data.narrative:
Substrate, a Series A semiconductor company founded by James Proud and Oliver Proud, has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 12 same-sector peers (3 public: ALAB, NVDA, AMD; 9 private including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor), though narrowly-filtered peer sets proved insufficient for direct median-based triangulation.

Of the three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression analysis was applicable. Using the $100M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage step-ups yields $200M. Public Semiconductors peers trade at a median 21.4x price-to-sales, but without disclosed revenue for Substrate, this anchor cannot be operationalized. The private peer universe exists but contains insufficient same-stage and similar-tier comparables to support a robust median approach.

The single-method triangulation yields a median valuation of $200M, with a range of $170M to $230M reflecting methodological conservatism around stage-progression assumptions. The primary uncertainty is the absence of revenue data; disclosing this would enable public-comp anchoring and narrow the valuation band. Stage-up multiples also vary materially by investor quality and market conditions, introducing model sensitivity. This range should be treated as preliminary pending additional financial transparency or a broader private peer dataset.
